title: Quedarse for Resulting States, Loss, and Deprivation

sections.content:
Use **quedarse + adjetivo / participio** when a state is the direct *consequence* of a preceding event, often involving loss, surprise, or physical disablement:

• **Reaction to news/shock**: *Se quedó sorprendido / boquiabierto.* (He was stunned / open-mouthed.) *Me quedé mudo.* (I was struck dumb.)
• **Loss / Deprivation**: *Se quedó sin dinero / sin trabajo / calvo.* (He was left without money / jobless / went bald.)
• **Physical conditions**: *Se quedó sordo / ciego.* (He went deaf / blind.)
• **Sleep**: *Se quedó dormido en el sofá.* (He fell asleep on the couch).

sections.title: Rules and Patterns
rows: to run out of / be left without

items.spanish: Me quedé dormido y llegué tarde a la oficina.
items.english: I overslept / fell asleep and arrived late at the office.

items.spanish: Al oír la noticia, todos nos quedamos boquiabiertos.
items.english: Upon hearing the news, we were all left open-mouthed.

items.spanish: Mi abuelo se quedó completamente sordo a los ochenta años.
items.english: My grandfather went completely deaf at age eighty.

sections.content: *Quedarse* always emphasizes the resulting aftermath of an event: *¿Cómo te quedaste? —Me quedé de piedra.*
